resultJson.description: Verified: the only git.push() in the codebase runs inside the 'Push branch' stage body (flow/src/main/scala/orca/pr/openPrFromBranch.scala:34), and stage bodies run before their own commit (runStage, flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala:86-90), so the push precedes that stage's commit, the two later stage commits, and teardown. teardownSuccess (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala:879-899) removes the progress log and commits but never pushes — the removal never reaches the PR, violating ADR 0018 R26 ('a merged PR must not contain the progress log'), confirmed by 545a065d cleaning it off master. Fix: after the cleanup commit in teardownSuccess, best-effort push — gated not merely on 'has upstream' but on 'the upstream tree contains the progress-log file', which is exactly when the push is needed and avoids surprise-publishing local commits of a reused --skip-branch branch that tracked a remote before the run. Decisions on the report's open questions: extra trailing commits on an already-open PR are acceptable (squashing would rewrite history + force-push, which R26 explicitly rejected and which would break commit-based resume); merge-commit repos need nothing further (once the removal is on the pushed tip, the merged tree lacks the file under any merge strategy).

tasks.title: Add GitTool.upstreamHas(path) probe with OsGitTool implementation and tests
tasks.description: In tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitTool.scala, add a READ-ONLY best-effort trait method `def upstreamHas(path: os.Path): Boolean` — true iff the current branch has an upstream and the upstream's tree contains `path` (relativized against the repo root). Returns false on no upstream, no remote, or any error; document it in the style of the existing `isIgnored`/`defaultBranch` docs ('best-effort, never for decisions that must be right' — it only gates a cosmetic teardown push). Implement in OsGitTool (same file) via exit-code of e.g. `git cat-file -e @{upstream}:<relpath>`, relativizing with the tool's workDir. No fake updates needed: the only other GitTool implementor is the test fake in flow/src/test/scala/orca/pr/OpenPrFromBranchTest.scala:46, which delegates via `export underlying.*` and picks the method up automatically — verify this compiles. Tests in tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/OsGitToolTest.scala reusing the bare-local-remote pattern at line 311 (`git init --bare` temp dir + `git remote add origin`): (1) no upstream → false; (2) file committed and pushed → true; (3) pushed but path absent from upstream tree → false.

tasks.title: Push the progress-log removal in teardownSuccess, with lifecycle test and doc updates
tasks.description: In runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala teardownSuccess (lines 879-899), add a third leg after 'commit progress-log removal', inside the `try` and before the `finally` (HEAD must still be on the feature branch — finishBranch in the finally may switch away): `bestEffort("push progress-log removal"): if git.upstreamHas(setup.store.path) then git.push().orThrow`. The minted WorkspaceWrite at the top of the method already covers push; gating on remote state (not on whether the commit leg succeeded) is robust to NothingToCommit on a resumed teardown. Update the method's scaladoc. Tests in runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala using the direct-invocation style at line 2157 (GitRepo.seeded() + OsGitTool + hand-built FlowSetup, ProgressStore.default for the store): (1) with a bare local remote and the progress file committed+pushed, teardownSuccess leaves the remote branch tip without the file; (2) with no upstream, teardownSuccess performs no push (remote absent/unchanged). Docs, kept concise per repo style: README.md 'Success teardown' bullet (~line 324) and the sentence at line 143 — note the removal commit is also pushed when the run had pushed the branch; adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md — one-sentence amendments to R5 (~line 394) and R26 (~line 658) recording the gated teardown push, noting R6 ('no runtime-imposed terminal push') is preserved because the push only completes a publication the flow itself already made. Finish with `sbt --client scalafmtAll` and a zero-warning compile.

resultJson.brief:
Orca is a direct-style Scala 3 project (Ox, munit) with modules tools/, flow/, runner/. MANDATORY: load the `direct-style-scala` skill (Skill tool) before writing or reviewing any Scala code — CLAUDE.md requires this of every subagent. Style: braceless syntax, explicit return types on public members, scaladoc on non-obvious members focusing on usage/invariants (never implementation history), zero-warning compile, format with `sbt --client scalafmtAll`. Comment style memory: comments must state only file-local facts, no exposition or history.

Key code, all paths verified:
- tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitTool.scala — `trait GitTool` (line 89) with `push()(using WorkspaceWrite): Either[PushFailure, Unit]` (line 152; argv is `git push -u origin HEAD`, see pushArgs line 706-724, so upstream is set on first push), READ-ONLY probes `isIgnored` (line 161) and `defaultBranch` (line 168) whose doc style the new `upstreamHas` should mirror. `OsGitTool` (same file, workDir field) is the real impl.
- flow/src/main/scala/orca/Flow.scala:79-92 — `runStage` runs the stage body, THEN `recordAndCommit`; this ordering is why the push inside the 'Push branch' stage body (flow/src/main/scala/orca/pr/openPrFromBranch.scala:33-34, the codebase's only push call site) precedes all subsequent commits.
- runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala — `teardownSuccess` (879-899): mints `given WorkspaceWrite = RuntimeInStage.workspaceToken()`, then bestEffort legs 'remove progress log' and 'commit progress-log removal' inside a try, with `finishBranch` in the finally (may checkout the start branch or delete a throwaway branch — so the new push leg must run before the finally). `bestEffort(what)(op)` (863-868) catches NonFatal and debug-logs; `.orThrow` inside it is the intended failure path. `setup.store.path` is the absolute os.Path of the progress-log file.
- tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitHubTool.scala:149-152 — createPr doc already states commits after the last push aren't included; stays valid.

Tests:
- tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/OsGitToolTest.scala:311-326 — established bare-local-remote push test pattern (`git init --bare` in a TempDirs dir, `git remote add origin <path>`, then `git.push().orThrow`; no credentials needed).
- runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala:2134-2161 — direct `FlowLifecycle.teardownSuccess(git, setup, returnToStartBranch = false)` invocation pattern: `GitRepo.seeded()` (helper in tools/src/test/scala/orca/testkit/GitRepo.scala), `new OsGitTool(workDir)`, `ProgressStore.default(workDir, prompt)`, hand-built `FlowLifecycle.FlowSetup(store, featureBranch, startBranch, stackSettings, branchMode)`, `given WorkspaceWrite = WorkspaceWrite.unsafe`.
- flow/src/test/scala/orca/pr/OpenPrFromBranchTest.scala:46-51 — fake GitTool delegates with `export underlying.*` minus overridden members, so a new trait method implemented on OsGitTool needs no fake changes.

Design rationale to preserve in code/docs: gate the teardown push on `upstreamHas(progressLogPath)` rather than mere upstream existence — a reused (--skip-branch) branch may have tracked a remote before the run, and pushing the run's local commits unasked would be a surprise side effect; whereas any push made BY the run necessarily carried the progress file (the header is committed before any stage, and every stage commit force-adds the log — see forceAdd doc, GitTool.scala:133-138, and ADR 0018 R8). Docs to touch: README.md line 143 and the 'Success teardown' bullet ~line 324; adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md R5 (~394), R26 (~658), R6 (~409, 'no runtime-imposed terminal push' — the amendment should note the gated push only completes a publication the flow already made). Do not propose history rewriting or force-push: R26 explicitly chose not to rewrite history, resume depends on commits, and the user forbids force-pushes. sbt-running work is slow (8-15 min); background it where possible and run one implementer at a time.
